import { Tabs, TabItem, Steps, LinkButton } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This guide walks through the pieces you need before a team goes out into the field: an API key, an SDK, a survey and at least one device. It takes about ten minutes.

If you only want to try Fieldkit from a terminal, skip ahead to [setting up the Fieldkit CLI](#setting-up-the-fieldkit-cli).

## Install the SDK

<Tabs syncKey="language">
  <TabItem label="Python" icon="seti:python">
  ```bash
  pip install fieldkit
  ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="TypeScript" icon="seti:typescript">
  ```bash
  npm install @fieldkit/sdk
  ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Configure your API key

The SDK reads `FIELDKIT_API_KEY` from the environment. You can also pass the key explicitly; see [Configuration](#configuration-options) below for every option.

```bash
export FIELDKIT_API_KEY=fk_live_...
```

:::note
Keys are scoped to a workspace. A key created in one workspace cannot read surveys or devices in another, even if you belong to both.
:::

### Configuration options

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| ------ | -------------------- | ------- |
| `api_key` | `FIELDKIT_API_KEY` | — |
| `api_url` | `FIELDKIT_API_URL` | `https://api.fieldkit.example` |
| `region` | `FIELDKIT_REGION` | `eu` |
| `timeout` | `FIELDKIT_TIMEOUT` | `30` |

## Create a survey

A survey is a versioned list of questions. Devices download the version that was current when they last synced.

```python
from fieldkit import Fieldkit

fk = Fieldkit()
survey = fk.surveys.create(
    name="water-quality-2025",
    questions=[
        {"id": "site", "type": "text", "required": True},
        {"id": "ph", "type": "number", "min": 0, "max": 14},
        {"id": "photo", "type": "image"},
    ],
)
```

## Register a device

```python
device = fk.devices.register(name="tablet-07", labels={"team": "north"})
```

The device is now visible on the dashboard and will pick up `water-quality-2025` on its next sync. See [Device Management](/docs/device-management) for the full lifecycle.

## Setting up the Fieldkit CLI

<Steps>

1. Install the CLI with Homebrew:

   ```bash
   brew install fieldkit/tap/fieldkit
   ```

2. Log in. The CLI opens a browser and stores the key in the [configuration file](/docs/configuration#configuration-file):

   ```bash
   fieldkit login
   ```

3. Check that it can see your devices:

   ```bash
   fieldkit devices list
   ```

</Steps>
